{{Short description|Set of mathematical conjectures proposed by  Douglas Ravenel}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Ravenel conjectures''' are a set of mathematical conjectures in the field of [[stable homotopy theory]] posed by [[Douglas Ravenel]] at the end of a paper published in 1984.<ref>{{cite journal | url = https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/mypapers/loc.pdf | title = Localization with Respect to Certain Periodic Homology Theories |  first = Douglas C. | last = Ravenel | journal = American Journal of Mathematics | volume =  106 | issue = 2 |  year = 1984 | pages = 351–414 | jstor = 2374308 | mr = 0737778 | doi=10.2307/2374308}}</ref> It was earlier circulated in preprint.<ref name=Hopkins>{{cite journal | url =http://www.intlpress.com/HHA/v10/n3/a1/v10n3a1.pdf | journal = Homology, Homotopy and Applications | volume = 10 | year = 2008 | issue = 3, ''Proceedings of a Conference in Honor of Douglas C. Ravenel and [[W. Stephen Wilson]]'' | pages = 1–13 | title = The mathematical work of Douglas C. Ravenel | last = Hopkins | first = Michael J.| doi = 10.4310/HHA.2008.v10.n3.a1 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The problems involved have largely been resolved, with all but the "telescope conjecture" being proved in later papers by others.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Devinatz | first1=Ethan S. | last2=Hopkins | first2=Michael J. |authorlink2=Michael J. Hopkins| last3=Smith | first3=Jeffrey H. | title=Nilpotence and stable homotopy theory. I | doi=10.2307/1971440 | mr=960945 | year=1988 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | issn=0003-486X | volume=128 | issue=2 | pages=207–241| jstor=1971440 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |jstor=120991|title=Nilpotence and Stable Homotopy Theory II | last1=Hopkins | first1=Michael J. |authorlink1=Michael J. Hopkins| last2=Smith | first2=Jeffrey H.  | year = 1998 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | volume = 148 | issue = 1 | pages = 1–49|doi=10.2307/120991 |citeseerx=10.1.1.568.9148 }}</ref><ref name=Hopkins/> Ravenel's conjectures exerted influence on the field through the founding of the approach of [[chromatic homotopy theory]].

The first of the seven conjectures, then the ''nilpotence conjecture'', was proved in 1988 and is now known as the [[nilpotence theorem]]. 

The '''telescope conjecture''', which was fourth on the original list, remains of substantial interest because of its connection with the convergence of an [[Adams–Novikov spectral sequence]]. While opinion has been generally against the truth of the original statement, investigations of associated phenomena (for a [[triangulated category]] in general) have become a research area in its own right.<ref>{{cite thesis | last = Brüning | first = Kristian | url = https://pace.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/pace/IRTG/PhD_Thesis/k1_m60.pdf | title = Subcategories of Triangulated Categories and the Smashing Conjecture | page=25| publisher = Dissertation zur Erlangung des akademischen Grades| year = 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jack|first1=Hall|last2=David|first2=Rydh|date=2016-06-27|title=The telescope conjecture for algebraic stacks|journal=Journal of Topology|volume=10|issue=3|pages=776–794|arxiv=1606.08413|language=en|doi=10.1112/topo.12021|s2cid=119336098 }}</ref>

On June 6, 2023, Robert Burklund, Jeremy Hahn, Ishan Levy, and [[Tomer Schlank]] announced a disproof of the telescope conjecture.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartnett |first=Kevin |date=2023-08-22 |title=An Old Conjecture Falls, Making Spheres a Lot More Complicated |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/an-old-conjecture-falls-making-spheres-a-lot-more-complicated-20230822/ |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref> Their preprint was submitted to the [[arXiv]] on October 26, 2023.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Burklund |first1=Robert |last2=Hahn |first2=Jeremy |last3=Levy |first3=Ishan |last4=Schlank |first4=Tomer |title=K-theoretic counterexamples to Ravenel's telescope conjecture |date=2023 |class=math.AT |eprint=2310.17459 }}</ref>
